diagnostic_evidence.quote: $c$ in the equation \cref{eq:ell1} is proportional to $\sigma$.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated proportionality permits c=-σ. Even on a sign-fitted uniform mesh, take v supported in a positive-phase cell. Then s(πv,πTv)=-||πv||²_s, whereas the asserted lower bound, reading the projection notation consistently as π, becomes positive for sufficiently large Υ and nonzero πv. The absolute-value spectral problem does not correct the sign of the subsequent signed stabilization.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State explicitly that c=ρσ with ρ>0 throughout this analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The stabilization coercivity and the localization and discrete-stability arguments are not established for all proportional coefficients allowed by the text.
issues.title: Signed stabilization requires positive, not merely arbitrary, proportionality
issues.why_classification: This standard local sign condition matches the explicitly specified benchmarks and preserves the intended same-sign-phase method and convergence rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: let $\mathcal{K}_H$ be a standard  quadrilateralization of the domain $\Omega$ with the mesh size $H$.
Here, the terms $\mathcal{Q}_H \pi v_1$ and $\mathcal{Q}_H \pi v_2$ vanish because $\pi v=0$ on each coarse element, and meanwhile $\mathcal{Q}_H\pi v|_{K_i}$ depends only on $\pi v|_{K_i}$.

issues.failure_explanation: No condition prevents a coarse cell from crossing the sign interface. On such a cell, π does not commute with sign restriction, and πv=0 does not imply πv₁=πv₂=0. The signed auxiliary mass can even be singular: on one square cell take σ=c=A on a strip of width 1/(A+1), and σ=c=-1 elsewhere, with l_*=1. Then ∫c=0, so s vanishes on the constant auxiliary space despite arbitrarily large Υ. Reflection into an adjacent equal-width strip has both stated reflection norms equal to one; for a fixed test function away from that strip, the claimed stabilization lower bound becomes positive as A grows while its left side remains zero. The corresponding zero basis right-hand sides also defeat the converse in lm3.2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require every coarse element to be sign-homogeneous. Retaining cut coarse cells instead requires a different projection or stabilization and a replacement analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The kernel correction, signed stabilization, basis-space characterization, and ensuing error analysis do not cover the permitted unfitted-interface meshes.
issues.title: The projection arguments silently require sign-fitted coarse cells
issues.why_classification: The source-supported restriction removes the unfitted heterogeneous-interface regime; preserving that regime requires a new construction and substantial replacement analysis.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated reflection norm is unweighted, whereas the s norm includes the varying factor Diam(K_i)^(-2). No mesh/reflection compatibility is assumed. For reflection between equal-shaped regions, with positive-side cell diameter H and reflected negative-side diameter h, a function supported on the positive side can satisfy ||Tv||²_s/||v||²_s=1+4(H/h)²/Υ even when ||R||₀=1. This exceeds the displayed bound when h is sufficiently small.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume uniform coarse-cell diameters, or impose mesh-weight comparability under reflection and include its factor in the s-norm bounds and resolution constants.
issues.overall_effect: The stated s-norm constants and the resolution estimates using them are unjustified on the general coarse meshes described.
issues.title: Unweighted reflection bounds do not control the mesh-weighted s norm
issues.why_classification: A standard mesh condition and routine weight-factor adjustment preserve the method, rates, and uniform-grid numerical setting.

issues.failure_explanation: No nonresonance or continuous inf-sup hypothesis is imposed. An explicit permitted example is the square split at y=1/2, with σ=c=A above and -1 below. Put q=sin(πx)sin(2πy), w=-q above and Aq below. Its trace and flux match, and B(w,v)=0 for every v when k²=5π², for arbitrarily large Υ=A. Refining H enforces the resolution condition but does not remove this kernel; generally πw≠0. Thus the converse fails, and stability on ker π alone cannot imply stability on the global coarse space.

issues.failure_explanation: For a boundary coarse cell, successive containing patches share points of ∂Ω, so the distance between their full boundaries is zero. Also, a finite coarse mesh cannot support an indefinitely strictly expanding sequence with positive boundary separation; after a patch reaches Ω, the stated inequality fails again. Thus the local-operator construction has no patch family satisfying its literal specifications for all claimed indices.

issues.failure_explanation: Small C_* and small Λ⁻¹ do not imply C_*Λ<C₂. In particular, increasing Λ can make p₂=C₂-C_*Λ negative. The kernel resolution condition only controls the energy component; the full augmented problem also has a projected-mass component that must be absorbed. The division by C and the subsequent contraction therefore lack a positive lower bound in the stated parameter regime.

issues.failure_explanation: For an individual i, the preceding product ||z_i||_s||z||_s cannot be replaced by ||z||²_s: the z_i may cancel in their sum. Moreover, a two-component lower bound requires the smaller coefficient, not their maximum.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Sum the signed mass terms before taking absolute values: isolate k²(cz,Tz) once and estimate the remaining cutoff terms locally. Then absorb the single global term using the minimum of the two valid coercivity margins.
